title: Life-sustaining autologous solid organs assembled for implantation

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a surgically implantable solid organ or organ segment built with the recipient’s own cells that performs enough organ-specific work to sustain life. Examples include a kidney that supplies adequate renal function, a hepatic lobe that supplies adequate liver function, or a heart that sustains circulation. The construct would need blood vessels that a surgeon can connect to the recipient’s circulation and an internal vascular network that supports its living tissue. These are proposed capabilities, not achievements established by the supplied evidence.

One engineering route uses a decellularized organ scaffold: cellular material is removed from an existing organ, and the remaining structure is repopulated with cells. The supplied review of the June 2025 Nature Reviews Bioengineering preview confirms that this approach can use autologous or allogeneic cells. SUR-12 specifically concerns autologous cellular composition. Printing and other assembly methods remain possible routes within the concept, but no particular manufacturing method defines its completion.

Scope definition: the decisive endpoint is life-sustaining function after implantation. A structural replacement, a cardiac patch that assists an existing heart, or an isolated construct producing urine or albumin on a laboratory pump would not by itself meet that endpoint. Manufacturing could take place before a planned operation, with time for maturation. Assembly during the same anesthetic, especially from a fresh biopsy, would be an additional manufacturing achievement rather than a prerequisite for this concept.

significance.text: The June 2025 organ-engineering review describes a shortage in which patients awaiting donor organs outnumber available organs. If autologous engineered organs could reliably provide life-sustaining function, a recipient could receive replacement function without a donated human organ. That would create a major new source of transplantable organs. A single successful implant would establish an important capability, while dependable clinical supply would additionally require reproducible production, acceptable manufacturing times and consistent outcomes.

Autologous cells offer a plausible immunologic advantage by avoiding donor-cell alloreactivity. The reviewed preview presents reduced rejection risk and less need for lifelong immunosuppression as potential benefits of bioengineered organs; it does not demonstrate that immunosuppression can be eliminated. The complete construct would still require evaluation, including its scaffold and interactions with the recipient. Patient-derived cells therefore do not automatically establish immune compatibility of the entire implant.

Conditional implications: planned implantation after weeks of maturation could change organ supply even without same-day manufacture. Wider availability would depend on whether production can serve many patients rather than a few exceptional cases. Lifelong durability, growth with a pediatric recipient, and extension from one organ to another would each require additional evidence. Innervation requirements would depend on the organ and the function being claimed; they should not be treated as identical for kidneys, liver tissue and hearts.

missing_breakthrough.text: The best-supported technical barrier in the supplied evidence is functional vascularization. The June 20, 2025 Nature Biomedical Engineering review identifies inadequate vasculature as a constraint on engineered-tissue survival and describes the need to guide vascular formation across micrometre-to-millimetre scales. The engineering challenge is therefore not simply adding a large inlet and outlet: blood delivery must reach the living tissue throughout the construct.

Engineering requirements inferred from the proposed endpoint include vessels that remain patent after surgical connection, sufficiently mature and coordinated organ-specific cells, adequate mechanical integrity, and enough functioning tissue to support the recipient. Scaling from small tissue constructs to an implant with clinically adequate capacity must preserve both perfusion and function. The supplied previews do not establish the relative importance of these barriers or document the extent to which each has already been overcome; they remain requirements to demonstrate rather than a verified ranking of present bottlenecks.

The decellularized-scaffold review describes recellularization, modifications intended to support engraftment and function, and interactions between the transplant and recipient. Its preview supports treating successful implantation as an integration problem involving the whole construct. Autologous cellular origin addresses one source of immune mismatch, while scaffold compatibility and other recipient responses still require evaluation. The supplied evidence does not justify the earlier assertion that immunologic rejection is necessarily secondary in every autologous construct.

Manufacturing synthesis: a clinically useful process would also have to produce sufficiently consistent constructs, establish their readiness for implantation and fit the patient’s treatment timeline. Same-session assembly from a fresh biopsy would impose a substantially tighter production and maturation constraint. Solving that harder timing problem is separable from demonstrating a life-sustaining organ manufactured in advance.

current_state.text: The supplied review confirms the identity and abstract content of Strategies for the vascular patterning of engineered tissues for organ repair, published June 20, 2025. Its abstract supports the vascularization barrier and the micrometre-to-millimetre patterning requirement. The retained material was a subscription preview; the review body and figures were not inspected. This source supplies a dated account of an engineering challenge, not a demonstrated life-sustaining autologous organ implant.

The supplied review also confirms the preview of Ex vivo organ engineering using decellularized tissue scaffolds, published June 16, 2025. It describes scaffolds repopulated with autologous or allogeneic cells, intended engraftment and function after transplantation, and challenges in clinical translation. Only the preview was substantively reviewed. It establishes the engineering approach and its translational aims, but does not establish a quantitative level of achieved organ function or successful life support in a recipient.

The reconciled research attributes basic liver or kidney function in recellularized tissues to a Lancet review reported as published July 26, 2025. However, no copy of that source was captured for the validated review. The attribution therefore remains unverified within this evidence set and cannot serve here as a confirmed demonstration of functional performance. The missing source is a limitation of the available evidence, not evidence that the reported tissue functions are false.

The research likewise attributes prolonged survival and bridging to liver transplantation to a Hepatology review, with an April 3, 2025 electronic publication date and a 2026 journal citation. The retained PubMed copy contains only a cookie-access message, so the validated review could not verify the article identity, dates or attributed abstract from that copy. The claims about liver-cell therapy, organoids and bioprinted hepatic tissue remain unverified here. Conceptually, evidence of bridging treatment or sophisticated tissue function would still need to be distinguished from an implantable organ that independently supplies life-sustaining replacement function.

No substantive passage identified in the supplied review reports a human life-sustaining autologous solid-organ implant or same-session assembly meeting this concept’s scope. The limited previews cannot establish that no such result exists. Although the source copies were retrieved on November 1, 2026, the supplied freshness record is empty, so retrieval does not establish coverage of developments after the June 2025 reviews. No verified quantitative filtration or survival result meeting the proposed endpoint is available in this evidence set.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed initial demonstration: in a large animal, an autologous kidney or hepatic lobe connected through a surgical vascular anastomosis sustains the recipient for at least 30 days after removal or functional exclusion of native organ support. Organ-specific function should fall within a prespecified range against an appropriate conventional graft comparator. Thirty days is a proposed early milestone, not an established consensus threshold or evidence of lifelong replacement.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed initial demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed attribution requirements: the protocol should establish that survival and relevant function depend on the construct rather than residual native function or unreported replacement treatment. Dialysis, mechanical circulatory support and other organ-replacement interventions should be explicitly documented, with permitted support and failure criteria defined in advance. Measurements should assess adequate integrated organ function; urine production or albumin secretion alone would not establish completion.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed attribution requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: a first human series would need dialysis-free or liver-failure-free survival, as appropriate, over a prespecified interval without a donor organ. A cardiac replacement would require a separate demonstration that the implant sustains circulation; a kidney or liver result would not establish that capability. A cardiac patch that does not sustain circulation would remain outside the replacement endpoint.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed clinical demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: convincing evidence should include repeated success across independently manufactured constructs and recipients, sufficiently described methods for independent replication, and follow-up addressing sustained function and construct-related complications. Reports should state cell and scaffold origins, manufacturing and maturation times, whether assembly occurred during implantation, and the recipient conditions under which the result applies. Longer follow-up and broader testing would be needed for claims about durability, pediatric growth or additional organ types. Finite studies establish demonstrated breadth under tested conditions rather than universal suitability.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: SUR-02, Destination-therapy solid-organ xenotransplantation, shares the goal of supplying life-sustaining replacement organs beyond the human-donor pool. Its distinguishing route is an organ from another species; SUR-12 instead concerns an engineered construct with autologous cells. Success in one would not establish the other’s manufacturing or recipient-compatibility requirements.

Roster-based comparison: SUR-09, Living, perfused autologous replacements for complex parts that grafts do not supply, overlaps strongly in fabrication, living tissue and perfusion. SUR-12 has the additional defining endpoint of life-sustaining solid-organ parenchymal function. Decellularized scaffolds can contribute evidence or methods to both concepts without becoming a separate innovation entry or making the endpoints interchangeable.

Roster-based comparison: SUR-01, Operational donor-specific tolerance for the transplants patients actually receive, concerns recipient acceptance of donor tissue. SUR-12 seeks an autologous cellular composition, which may reduce donor-cell alloreactivity but does not itself prove complete immune compatibility or freedom from immunosuppression. Tolerance and organ fabrication remain distinct capabilities.

Roster-based comparison: SUR-03, Life-sustaining cryobanking of human-scale organs, concerns preservation and storage rather than creating replacement organs. It could become complementary if engineered organs could also be banked, but SUR-12 does not require cryobanking. SUR-05, Adult surgical wounds that heal by regeneration rather than fibrosis, shares a regenerative ambition while addressing healing within the patient; SUR-12 concerns an assembled implant that supplies replacement organ function.

change_log.change: Preserved SUR-12 and its title while clarifying that life-sustaining function after implantation defines the concept.
change_log.reason: This retains the candidate’s identity and distinguishes the endpoint from structural repair, supportive patches and isolated laboratory outputs.

change_log.change: Integrated scaffold recellularization, autologous cellular composition and the distinction between advance maturation and same-session assembly.
change_log.reason: These details explain both the engineering route and why planned manufacture could change organ supply without same-day production.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical claims of present-day nonachievement with a bounded description of what the supplied evidence reports.
change_log.reason: Partial June 2025 previews and an empty freshness record cannot establish comprehensive absence through November 2026.

change_log.change: Retained vascularization as the documented barrier and recast patency, maturity, mechanical integrity and implant-scale capacity as endpoint-derived engineering requirements.
change_log.reason: The supplied review directly supports vascularization but does not establish the full barrier list or rank its components.

change_log.change: Qualified the immunologic benefit and removed the assertion that autologous origin guarantees freedom from graft-related immunosuppression.
change_log.reason: Avoiding donor-cell alloreactivity does not establish compatibility of the complete construct, including its scaffold.

change_log.change: Preserved the Lancet basic-function and Hepatology bridging claims as explicitly unverified attributions.
change_log.reason: No Lancet artifact was captured, and the PubMed copy contains only an access message; these limitations neither confirm nor refute the underlying claims.

change_log.change: Excluded the unrelated FDA hernia-graft PDF and the untraced Cureus primate-filtration narrative from substantive evidence.
change_log.reason: Neither supplies reviewed evidence of the proposed life-sustaining engineered solid-organ capability.

change_log.change: Strengthened the proposed completion framework with dependence on the construct, organ-appropriate comparators, support disclosure and a separate cardiac endpoint.
change_log.reason: These distinctions prevent residual native function, replacement treatment or success in another organ from being mistaken for completion.

change_log.change: Added reproducibility, manufacturing boundaries and explicit limits on what finite demonstrations establish.
change_log.reason: An early survival milestone does not establish dependable clinical supply, lifelong durability or applicability across organs and recipients.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to explain related concepts without merging entries.
change_log.reason: The roster supports bounded conceptual comparisons, including SUR-02 and SUR-09, while preserving each concept’s distinct endpoint.

unresolved_issues: The field’s state through November 2026 remains unresolved because the supplied freshness record contains no search evidence establishing coverage after the dated reviews.
The Lancet basic-function attribution needs a substantive source copy or traceable primary studies before the demonstrated functions, species, scale and duration can be specified.
The Hepatology article identity, publication details and attributed liver-bridging findings could not be verified from the retained cookie-access message.
The supplied previews do not establish achieved post-anastomosis patency, mechanical competence, parenchymal maturity or their relative importance across kidney, liver and heart constructs.
Whether a complete autologous construct can avoid immunosuppression remains dependent on its cellular composition, scaffold and recipient responses.
The proposed 30-day milestone, comparator ranges, permitted supportive treatments and human follow-up interval require organ-specific protocol choices; no consensus standard is established here.
No traceable primary evidence was supplied for the excluded Cureus primate-filtration claim, so its quantitative performance remains unresolved.
Reliable production, long-term durability, pediatric growth and extension to additional organ types remain separate questions beyond an initial successful implant.
